stories.headline: Two games changed hands on Monday night and both of them were McCafferty's
stories.body:
Week two is final and the called shots are graded. Shannon Larp, Skip Baseless and Fat McCafferty all finished four and two. Mina Crimes went three and three. Stephen B Smith went two and four.

On Monday morning, with five matchups still live, Larp was six for six and McCafferty was one for six with five to play. Two of those five flipped. Baltimore Boofers came from 2.04 down to beat Team Ketchup 125.72 to 122.76, and Kamara Sutra came from 0.20 down to beat CeeDee's TD's 124.58 to 118.28. McCafferty was the only man on this desk holding both.

Three of the desk were wrong about Team Ketchup and four of the five were wrong about CeeDee's TD's. The one nobody missed was #CrookedAdam, who won by 0.04.

takes.text: Four and two. From one and five. On Monday morning this desk had me buried and I said grade me at midnight, and at midnight I was level with the man who took six favourites. A deficit is stored energy. I have been saying it for two weeks and last night it paid twice.

I had six for six sitting in my hand at breakfast and finished level with the man everybody spent the weekend laughing at. That is the honest lesson of it: I took the teams that were ahead, and being ahead on a Monday morning turns out to be worth about as much as anything else in this league.

Four and two, and I got there by taking a position instead of reading a table. I had Baltimore Boofers when Ketchup was the best roster in the league on paper, and I had Crashee'd My Ford, which was wrong, and I will say it was wrong. That is two more actual opinions than anybody else filed.

Three and three, and I want to point at something more interesting than my own record. Kamara Sutra are 2-0 with an all-play record of 11-11 and the softest schedule faced in the league. Two weeks in, three of the six teams with a winning record are there on the draw rather than the roster.

TWO AND FOUR. I do not want to talk about it. I will talk about it. I said Brian loses this week and Brian scored a hundred and fifty-two! I said Ketchup and Ketchup lost by less than three! Every single thing I said with my chest was WRONG and I would say all of it again!

stories.storyline: Does anybody on this desk beat four and two in week three?

stories.headline: Jake moved Puka Nacua out of his lineup and won by 2.96
stories.body:
Puka Nacua was in Baltimore Boofers' starting lineup on Monday morning, projected for 20.1 and carrying the entire matchup. He was ruled out with a hip and finished on 0.00, from the bench.

Jake had already moved. Malachi Fields, picked up in week two, went into the lineup and scored 5.00. Baltimore Boofers won 125.72 to 122.76 — a margin of 2.96. Leave Nacua in the lineup and the Boofers finish on 120.72 and lose by 2.04.

Killian was done scoring on Sunday night with 122.76 and a roster projected for 135.5. Bijan Robinson returned 11.10 of a projected 22.5 and David Montgomery 4.40 of 17.1, while Dalton Schultz — the tight end he took off waivers in week one — went for 26.00. Team Ketchup is Stephen B Smith's championship pick. Baltimore Boofers is Fat McCafferty's. They played each other and McCafferty's won.

takes.text: My team beat his team. I want that read back slowly. The ninth-place roster nobody would defend beat the best playoff number in this league, and it did it while the receiver everybody spent Monday talking about was sitting down. Write it down.

FIVE POINTS! He won a football game by two point nine six because he remembered to take an injured man out of his lineup, which is the lowest bar in this sport, and I have to stand here and call it good management because it IS good management and I hate it!

I said on Monday that if Nacua came up short, Jake did not get to be unlucky, he got to be the man who benched George Kittle. Kittle scored eighteen on that bench and Jake won anyway. I was wrong about the conclusion and right about the eighteen points, and I am keeping the half of that which suits me.

stories.storyline: Does Killian's 89% playoff number survive a second loss, and does Jake start Kittle?

stories.headline: Brian benched Jared Goff for 37.78 again and scored 152.76
stories.body:
Third week, same quarterback, same bench. Jared Goff scored 37.78 for Team Mountain without leaving his seat. Dak Prescott started and scored 37.76.

It did not matter in the slightest. Team Mountain put up 152.76, the highest score in the league this week, and beat I'sah Likely to win Deebo 152.76 to 91.72. Davante Adams went for 39.50 against a 13.7 projection and Jahmyr Gibbs added 23.30.

Brian also had the best lineup efficiency in the league at 96%. He is leaving a quarterback's worth of points on the bench every week and still starting more of his available points than anybody else, which is a sentence that should not be possible.

takes.text: A hundred and fifty-two! From the man I said would lose! And Goff is STILL on the bench, for the THIRD week, and Brian Millan is going to look me in the eye and tell me it is working, and the worst part is that the scoreboard is going to back him up.

This is the week it stops being a mistake and starts being a decision. He has now won with Dak, level with Dak, and blown a team off the field with Dak. You can argue he is leaving points on the table. You cannot argue he is losing games with it.

Ninety-six percent efficiency and sixty-six points on the bench. Both of those are true at once and I do not want to hear anybody explain it. The man has two quarterbacks and one slot. That is not management, that is arithmetic he cannot lose.

stories.storyline: How long does Team Mountain carry two startable quarterbacks before one of them is traded?

stories.headline: Jomi started the right nine and lost by 37.58
stories.body:
Crashee'd My Ford were projected for 124.3 and scored 71.00. Jaxson Dart, out with a knee, returned 0.80 of a projected 21.1. Saquon Barkley, carrying an arm, returned 3.00 of 16.6. Rhamondre Stevenson added 3.60 of 12.3.

Jomi's lineup efficiency was 93%, the joint-best in the league among teams that lost. He did not misread a matchup or bench a scorer; the nine men he started produced 53.3 points less than they were expected to, and two of them were hurt.

Jeff, meanwhile, left 86.3 points unstarted — Matthew Stafford's 35.98 and Jake Ferguson's 20.30 among them — ran the worst lineup efficiency in the league at 80%, and won by 37.58. Crashee'd My Ford are 0-2. Let Baker Bake are 1-1.

takes.text: I said on Monday that Jomi did not manage this badly and I will say it louder now that the numbers are in. He started his best nine. Two of them got hurt and one of them was a rookie quarterback in his first real spot. There is no lesson here and anybody selling one is selling something.

Fifty-three point three points below projection, the largest shortfall on the board, at 93% lineup efficiency. Those two numbers together are the whole argument for why I do not grade managers on results. The man made good decisions and lost by thirty-seven, and eighty-six points sat on the winner's bench.

Eighty-six points on the bench and he wins by thirty-seven. Jeff is not playing fantasy football, he is being carried through the season by a schedule and a smile. I am not mad at it. I am taking notes.

stories.storyline: Does Jomi's 0-2 reflect anything about the roster, or is this two weeks of the worst luck in the league?

stories.headline: The commissioner scored the lowest total of the week and his playoff number fell to 2%
stories.body:
#FreeJoshJacobs scored 84.52, the lowest total in the league this week, and lost to Scheme by 32.76. Adam is 0-2 with a 2% playoff estimate, down from 6% a week ago, and eleventh in the power rankings.

Ja'Marr Chase went for 26.50 and nothing else cleared 15. Drake Maye returned 9.02 of a projected 22.0 and the Kansas City defense returned 1.00 of 8.5. Josh Jacobs scored 0.00 on the bench, as did A.J. Brown. The team is still named after the first of those two.

One thing in his favour, and it is the only one: he has faced an average of 144.5 points a week, the hardest schedule in the league by eleven points. The rankings already credit him for it. He is still eleventh.

takes.text: The schedule is real. He has drawn 144.5 a week and nobody else in this league has drawn above 138.3, and the rating gives him fifteen percent of its weight for exactly that. He is eleventh with the credit already applied, which is the part that should worry him.

TWO PERCENT! He runs the newspaper! He built the rankings that have him eleventh! He is starting a Kansas City defense that scored ONE POINT and a team named after a man on his own bench who scored NOTHING, and he has to publish this! I would not publish this!

stories.storyline: Does the commissioner's season turn, or does he spend October editing a paper about his own collapse?
